rationale:
**Verdict:** the marked tests cover almost all of `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`. One stated obligation, that `text()` returns the selected text before redaction, has no test marked to this requirement.

**Obligations that are covered**

- **Selection from the root and the empty selector.**
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` selects every outline item by its selector. It asserts that `text()` equals the item's source span and that `structural_hash()` matches the item's.
  - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` and `explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme` select `""` and `part[selected]`.
- **Shared snapshot and fingerprinting rules.**
  - `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())` is asserted in the Markdown and Rust tests.
  - The custom-language test checks that the selected fingerprint scheme is retained, that two selections from different sources give equal fingerprints, and that a different scheme changes the fingerprint.
- **No extra file read, and the result outlives the original handle.**
  - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` drops `file` and then overwrites the file on disk.
  - It then checks that `selected_again.text()` is unchanged and that `selected.select("")` still returns the original `"first\nsecond\n"`.
  - `OutlineContent::from_id` fails after the edit, which confirms the contrast.
- **Selector syntax applied to selection.**
  - The Markdown test covers percent-encoded names, `#N` duplicates, and anonymous `section@` and `block@` hash selectors.
  - The CSS test covers `#N` numbering within each parent.
  - The plain-text tests cover `line@` selectors, and `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` covers identical lines.
- **Identical plain-text lines are interchangeable.** The `line` case of `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` checks that identical lines share a selector and that selecting that selector returns `"same"`. `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` does the same for `alpha`.
- **Errors.**
  - `missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors` checks that a malformed selector (`fn[`) and a missing one (`fn[absent]`) fail.
  - `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` checks that duplicated `part[same]` and non-identical `line[same]` selectors return an "ambiguous" error.
  - The CSS test checks that `rule[a%20b]` without `#N` fails.
- **`id()` and "including attached source".** `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` asserts `id()`. The Rust test asserts that the selected function text starts with the doc comment and contains `#[inline]`.

**Gap: `text()` before redaction**

The `select` and `text` declarations in the requirement say `text()` is the "Original selected text … before redaction." No test marked `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection` puts credential-shaped text in a selected item. A `select` that sliced the redacted text would pass every marked test.

The unmarked test `formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs` does check this. It asserts that `selected.text()` contains the raw token while `selected.format()` does not. It is marked only for `requirements.sdk.sources.redaction` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.node_contents`, so this is a marking gap against the subject. The fix is to add a `{test}` reference to `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection` on that test.

No `{fixme}` acknowledges this gap, so the determination is false.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineId;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
File-read and parsing failures return errors, distinct from successful contents
for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that language's parsing
rules; a parse failure is reported rather than interpreted as plain text.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
